result.content:
VERDICT: Proceed with log-only diagnostics joining model_skill forecast error by lead time to cal_err failures before any promotion or blend weight changes.

REASONING: Tree is settle_hour-only, so per-lead-time skill is invisible in current metrics; hourly_wx_axes and model_break_decay graduation requires evidence that calibration violations concentrate in specific hours/leads. A diagnostic cross-check (skill vs cal_err by lead hour) is zero-risk and directly gates whether blend or calibration fixes are the right lever. No promotion bar changes justified without that evidence.

NEXT_STEPS:
1. In model_skill.py, extend the forecast-error aggregation function (groupby lead_time / hours_to_settle) to emit per-lead MAE/RMSE to logs, keyed identically to cal_err records.
2. Add a join diagnostic (e.g., diagnostics/skill_vs_cal.py or in model_blend_diagnostic.py) that merges skill-by-lead with cal_err failure rows on (market, lead_hour) and logs the top-N violating hours sorted by |cal_err| and count.
3. In model_blend_*.py, log current blend weights and per-model contribution at the offending hours only — no weight mutation.
4. Gate hourly_wx_axes and model_break_decay autopilot graduation on the diagnostic output: require documented calibration-violating hours + stable skill per lead before allowing graduation criteria to be evaluated.
5. Add an assertion/log-warning when settle_hour-only tree masking hides >X% lead-time variance, so the limitation is surfaced in every run.

CALL_BACK_IF: Diagnostic shows calibration violations concentrated in identifiable lead hours AND model_skill confirms error growth at those leads, justifying a scoped calibration or blend proposal.
